collection_instructions: Collect blood in a plain red (no gel) or gold (SST) top tube. For red-top tube (no gel), allow blood to clot (10-15 minutes) at room temperature. Separate serum from cells and refrigerate.
storage_requirements: Ambient: 48 hours; Refrigerated: 7 days; Frozen: 60 days
notes: Avoid testing during acute illness as levels may be temporarily affected.

collection_instructions: Collect 1-2 mL of blood in a red-top tube (no additive).
storage_requirements: Room temperature: 5 days; Refrigerated: 7 days; Frozen: 90 days.
notes: Elevated RF levels can indicate rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune conditions.

collection_instructions: Collect blood in a gold-top SST tube. Allow the specimen to clot for 30 minutes at room temperature. Centrifuge to separate serum from cells.
storage_requirements: Store serum at room temperature for up to 7 days. For longer storage, refrigerate at 2-8°C for up to 14 days or freeze at -20°C for up to 6 months.
notes: Ensure the specimen is not hemolyzed, as this can affect test results.

collection_instructions: Collect 1 mL (0.5 mL minimum) serum in each of two separate red-top tubes (no gel).
storage_requirements: Transport refrigerated. Room temperature: 48 hours; Refrigerated: 7 days; Frozen: 1 year.
notes: Gross hemolysis; serum separator tube; received room temperature are unacceptable.

collection_instructions: Collect 1 mL of blood in a serum separator tube (SST). Allow the blood to clot at room temperature for 30 minutes, then centrifuge to separate the serum.
storage_requirements: Store serum at room temperature for up to 7 days, refrigerated for up to 7 days, or frozen for up to 30 days.
notes: Elevated CRP levels may indicate inflammation due to conditions such as bacterial infections, rheumatic fever, active arthritis, myocardial infarction, malignancies, and postoperative states. This test cannot detect small elevations of CRP associated with increased cardiovascular risk.

test_name: ESR; Sedimentation Rate by Modified Westergren
collection_instructions: Collect blood in a lavender-top EDTA tube. Invert gently to mix.
storage_requirements: Store at room temperature. Do not refrigerate.
notes: Perform the test within 4 hours of collection for optimal results.
Administration of STRENSIQ may interfere in certain assays and may falsely elevate values. For patients receiving STRENSIQ, consideration should be given to using alternate methods.

test_name: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Differential and Platelets
collection_instructions: Maintain specimen at room temperature. Do not refrigerate. If multiple draws are performed, collect EDTA (lavender-top) tube last.
notes: If abnormal cells are noted on a manual review of the peripheral blood smear or if the automated differential information meets specific criteria, a full manual differential will be performed.

collection_instructions: Fasting for at least 10-12 hours is required.
storage_requirements: Room Temperature 24 hours; Refrigerated 7 days; Frozen 28 days
notes: This test provides a comprehensive assessment of cardiovascular disease risk by measuring various lipid fractions and particle sizes.

collection_instructions: Collect 1-2 mL blood in a red-top tube (no additive).
storage_requirements: Room temperature: 7 days; Refrigerated: 7 days; Frozen: 28 days.
notes: Avoid hemolysis. Dietary supplements containing biotin may interfere in assays and may skew analyte results to be either falsely high or falsely low. For patients receiving the recommended daily doses of biotin, draw samples at least 8 hours following the last biotin supplementation. For patients on mega-doses of biotin supplements, draw samples at least 72 hours following the last biotin supplementation. Administration of STRENSIQ may interfere in certain assays and may falsely elevate values. For patients receiving STRENSIQ, consideration should be given to using alternate methods.

collection_instructions: Collect blood sample in a lavender-top EDTA tube.
storage_requirements: Store at room temperature; do not freeze.

collection_instructions: Collect 2 mL of serum; do not collect specimen after a transrectal biopsy, as results may be falsely elevated. Administration of STRENSIQ may interfere in certain assays and may falsely elevate values. For patients receiving STRENSIQ, consideration should be given to using alternate methods.
storage_requirements: Transport frozen; room temperature acceptable if received within 72 hours. Specimen stability: Room temperature: 72 hours; Refrigerated: 72 hours; Frozen: 5 months.
notes: Based on solid evidence, screening with PSA and/or DRE detects some prostate cancers that would never have caused important clinical problems.

collection_instructions: Collect blood sample in a lavender-top EDTA tube.
storage_requirements: Store at room temperature; process within 24 hours.

collection_instructions: No special preparation is usually required.
storage_requirements: Room temperature: 7 days; Refrigerated: 7 days; Frozen: 28 days
notes: Useful in screening for hyperthyroidism and diagnosing hypothyroidism.

collection_instructions: Collect 1 mL of serum; for pre-pubertal children, use test code 36087-FSH, Pediatrics assay.
storage_requirements: Room temperature: 7 days; Refrigerated: 7 days; Frozen: 28 days
notes: FSH is used in the diagnosis and management of infertility and in monitoring FSH suppressive therapy.

collection_instructions: Collect blood in a red-top tube (no gel). Allow blood to clot at room temperature. Centrifuge to separate the serum from the cells and immediately pour serum into a plastic transport tube.
storage_requirements: Room temperature: 7 days; Refrigerated: 21 days; Frozen: 2 years
notes: This test was developed and its analytical performance characteristics have been determined by Quest Diagnostics. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA. This assay has been validated pursuant to the CLIA regulations and is used for clinical purposes.

collection_instructions: Collect 1 mL of blood in a red-top tube (no gel). Allow blood to clot at room temperature for 30 minutes. Centrifuge and separate the serum from the cells.
storage_requirements: Room temperature: 7 days; Refrigerated: 14 days; Frozen: 6 months
notes: This test measures dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a potent androgen derived from testosterone via 5-Alpha-Reductase activity. Elevated DHT levels can indicate 5-Alpha-Reductase deficiency, which may result in incompletely virilized males (phenotypic females).

collection_instructions: Collect blood in a gold-top serum separator tube (SST).
storage_requirements: Store serum at room temperature or refrigerate. Do not freeze.

collection_instructions: Collect blood in a gold-top SST tube; allow to clot; centrifuge and separate serum from cells.
storage_requirements: Store serum at 2-8°C; do not freeze.
notes: Estradiol is a form of estrogen, a female sex hormone produced by the ovaries. It plays a key role in the development and maintenance of female reproductive tissues and secondary sexual characteristics.
